Subject: ACME - MSA redlines: pilot opt-out from auto-renew & TfC ask

Hi Stephanie / Laura / Aditya,

Thanks again for the time last week — we're excited to move the pilot forward. Attached is the MSA with our in-house redlines (ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and the draft Order Form. Two key asks from procurement/legal that we need your help on:

1) Auto-renew carve-out for the pilot: they want the pilot term explicitly excluded from the standard auto-renew clause so the pilot can end without triggering the committed term.
2) Termination for Convenience (TfC): they need a limited TfC for the pilot with a short notice/transition window, and an explicit obligation for data handback.

From their perspective it's a risk trade-off: they need enough flexibility to stop the pilot quickly if it fails, but they recognize we need clarity on what counts as the pilot scope.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a pilot carve-out and a pilot-specific TfC framed as a limited, one-time exit (not the same as enterprise TfC)? If so, please propose language we can pass to our GC.

Attachments: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx (docx), OrderForm_Acme_20250512.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,

Subject: Re: ACME - MSA redlines: pilot opt-out from auto-renew & TfC ask

Laura / Aditya — looping you in.

Quick context: Acme wants to ensure the pilot can be terminated without triggering our standard auto-renew/commit terms and is asking for a limited TfC for the pilot period plus data handback assurances. We should avoid making a permanent carve-out to the MSA that undermines standard renewal mechanics for paying customers.

Ask: Laura, can you draft a compact pilot carve-out clause (1–2 paragraphs) that:
- Excludes the pilot scope from auto-renew and committed term triggers;
- Limits TfC to pilot-specific services for a single off-ramp (not a perpetual right);
- Includes a 30–60 day data handback and deletion schedule;
- Keeps commercial exposure capped (no refund of previously consumed usage).

Aditya — please confirm that operationally we can support a 30-day versus 60-day handback and whether we should ask for a small pilot fee to offset the risk.

Target: send suggested clause back to ACME by EOD tomorrow so they can loop in GC early next week.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Stephanie / Aditya — draft language below. I kept it tight and operationally prescriptive to limit ambiguity. If you want, I can attach as a snippet file (pilot_carveout_snippet.txt) for them to insert.

-- suggested clause (for inclusion in MSA / Order Form) --
"Pilot Exclusion; Pilot Termination for Convenience. Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in this Agreement, the parties agree that the services expressly identified as the 'Pilot' in the Order Form (the "Pilot Services") shall be excluded from Section [Auto-Renew Section] and from provisions that would otherwise automatically extend or convert the Pilot Services into a Committed Term. Either party may terminate the Pilot Services for convenience upon providing thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party. Following termination of the Pilot Services for convenience, Redwood will, at Acme's option, (a) return a copy of Acme data in a standard, machine-readable format, or (b) securely delete Acme data in accordance with the Data Return & Deletion Schedule set forth in Exhibit X. Any fees paid for Pilot Services are non-refundable, provided that Redwood will reasonably cooperate with a negotiated offboarding scope to minimize customer operational impact."

Key notes / tradeoffs:
- I suggested 30 days for TfC (tight) to keep pilot nimble; 60 days is more customer-friendly but increases our operational window.
- I included a clear data-return/deletion callout to make the exit deterministic; recommend we bind Exhibit X to a template handback schedule.
- The clause explicitly carves the pilot out of auto-renew only; it does not permit repeated use of pilot-TfC to avoid converting pilots into a perpetual opt-out. That helps limit precedent risk.

If we accept 30 days, operationally we need Aditya to confirm we can complete data handback and any required KV-cache flushes within that window. Also confirm whether we should treat the pilot as a separate billing item (small non-refundable pilot fee) to discourage churn.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Thanks Laura — that draft looks reasonable and much clearer than our in-house redlines. A couple of quick requests from Acme GC:

1) They'd like the notice window for the pilot TfC to be 75 days instead of 30 — they want extra time to wind down dependencies on their side.
2) They want confirmation on the auto-renew mechanics: specifically, will Redwood send a renewal reminder 60 days before any non-pilot term that carries a renewal? If we can confirm reminder cadence and that the pilot is excluded from those reminders, that should resolve most of their concerns.

If Redwood can accept 75 days on the pilot TfC, Acme is willing to accept the non-refundable pilot fee proposal (small fixed amount) and will proceed to circulate to GC for a countersign. Alternatively, if 75 days is too long for Redwood, propose we land at 45 days and Acme will take back to GC as a middle ground.

Next steps: Stephanie / Aditya — please confirm preferred notice window (30 / 45 / 75) and whether Redwood will add a renewal reminder cadence note into the Order Form (we can add language like: "Redwood will provide written renewal notice at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of any non-pilot committed term"). We aim to get to countersign by the end of next week.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Director, Vendor Management — Acme Corporation
